books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Alexander Gardner, Antietam, Maryland: Confederate soldiers, photographed September 1862. Public domain. Image from the shared pool.
stimulus.text: The photograph shows dead Confederate soldiers in gray uniforms lying on the battlefield at Antietam, Maryland, in September 1862. It was taken by Alexander Gardner days after the battle, the first time Americans saw photographs of battlefield dead. Brady exhibited the photographs in New York in October 1862 as “The Dead of Antietam.”

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The photograph was taken days after the Battle of Antietam. It most directly supports which conclusion about the war by 1862?

options.text: The Union had already won the war.
options.misconception: Background: the war lasted until 1865. A photograph of dead men in 1862 shows a war still being fought.

options.text: Battles were fought far away from American civilians.
options.misconception: The dead lie in a Maryland field, and the photograph was shown to civilians in Northern cities.

options.text: The war had grown far bloodier than expected.
The Confederacy had no army left after Antietam.
options.misconception: Background: Lee’s army retreated in order and fought for two and a half more years.

rationales.A: Background: the war lasted until 1865. A photograph of dead men in 1862 shows a war still being fought.
rationales.B: The dead lie in a Maryland field, and the photograph was shown to civilians in Northern cities.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Antietam was the bloodiest single day of the Civil War.
rationales.D: Background: Lee’s army retreated in order and fought for two and a half more years.
rationales.general:
1. The photograph shows what newspapers could only describe: dead men lying in the grass.
2. Background from the books: in 1861 both sides expected a short, glorious war, over by Christmas.
3. Background from the books: Antietam was the bloodiest single day of the Civil War.
4. A single day’s killing, photographed and displayed, ended the idea of a painless war.
Remember: photographs of the dead ended the short-war dream faster than any speech.
